side_room_king.title: The Dorm Room King Contest
side_room_king.beats:
An evening in Heights Alliance, about a week after move-in. Class 1-A's dorm has stopped smelling of cardboard, and in the Class 1-A Dorm Lounge Mina Ashido announces that rooms this unpacked deserve judging. Toru Hagakure seconds it at once, Ochaco Uraraka is curious, Kyoka Jiro is reluctant and Momo Yaoyorozu asks what the scoring criteria will be. The women of the class will tour the men's wing door by door and crown a Room King.

Canon default course, as pressure the player can change: Izuku Midoriya tries to block his doorway and fails; every wall, shelf and pillow is All Might, and he goes scarlet while the judges count posters. Fumikage Tokoyami's black walls and skulls draw delighted squeals he does not appreciate. Yuga Aoyama's mirror ball dazzles the whole hallway. Eijiro Kirishima's punching bag and bold calligraphy are judged exactly what everyone expected. Denki Kaminari's trendy clutter is called trying too hard. Shoto Todoroki's tatami room, rebuilt in a single day, earns a stunned silence. Katsuki Bakugo is already asleep and his door stays shut. Then Rikido Sato opens his door on a chiffon cake cooling on the rack, offers slices, and the hungry judges hand him the crown. The men, Minoru Mineta loudest, demand a return tour of the women's wing; the women agree on their own terms, Jiro's guitars embarrass her and Yaoyorozu's canopy bed fills her whole room.

Sato's cake winning is only the default: a party room with a stronger showing, better snacks or a well-argued vote can take the crown, and the losers' complaints are half the fun.

By path: a 1-A student party is a judge, a contestant or both. The player's own room is ALWAYS a stop on the tour: the judges reach the player's door, the player shows it off or tries to hide it, and it gets scored and argued over like every other room, and the player gets a vote on the crown. A 1-B party hears the noise through the wall: Itsuka Kendo calls 1-B's own contest that same evening in the Class 1-B Dorm Lounge, Neito Monoma insists theirs will be far more refined, and it plays the same way, the player's room included.

The event is complete when a Room King is crowned, or the party leaves the dorm.
